headline_marked: [[Nationwide ambulance strike called off]] after government assurance to review demands within 30 days
headline: Nationwide ambulance strike called off after government assurance to review demands within 30 days
summary: The Bangladesh Ambulance Owners' Welfare Association ended their indefinite strike late Tuesday night, trusting the government's promise to address their demands and alleviate public suffering.
details: The Bangladesh Ambulance Owners' Welfare Association has called off its indefinite nationwide strike, following assurances from the government to address their demands. The decision was announced late Tuesday night at an emergency press conference in Dhaka.

Advocate Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, Chief Coordinator of Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal and a Member of Parliament, stated that the association's demands would be reviewed and a logical decision made within the next 30 days.

Md. Golam Mostofa Fuad, Chief Advisor of the Association, said they decided to withdraw the strike to avoid public suffering and out of trust in the government. He urged all ambulance owners and workers across the country to resume services immediately.

The association had previously called the strike to press for several demands, including commercial registration, implementation of commercial policies, parking facilities, toll-free passage for ambulances, and ensuring 24-hour fuel supply.
caption:
Good news for public health! The nationwide ambulance strike in Bangladesh has been called off, ending potential widespread disruption to medical services.

The Bangladesh Ambulance Owners' Welfare Association has called off its indefinite nationwide strike, following assurances from the government to address their demands. The decision was announced late Tuesday night at an emergency press conference in Dhaka.

Advocate Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas, Chief Coordinator of Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal and a Member of Parliament, stated that the association's demands would be reviewed and a logical decision made within the next 30 days.

Md. Golam Mostofa Fuad, Chief Advisor of the Association, said they decided to withdraw the strike to avoid public suffering and out of trust in the government. He urged all ambulance owners and workers across the country to resume services immediately.

The association had previously called the strike to press for several demands, including commercial registration, implementation of commercial policies, parking facilities, toll-free passage for ambulances, and ensuring 24-hour fuel supply.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: 2 killed, 25 injured as [[dispute over a signboard sparks bloody clashes]] in Bhairab
headline: 2 killed, 25 injured as dispute over a signboard sparks bloody clashes in Bhairab
summary: A road safety sign mentioning only one village's name has torn apart decades of social harmony between Akbarnagar and Mirarchar villages.
details: Two people, Masud and Hiron, were killed and at least 25 others injured in violent clashes between residents of Akbarnagar and Mirarchar villages in Bhairab, Brahmanbaria.

// This is a clash over a signboard. It started in July 2023 when the Roads and Highways Department installed a sign reading 'Akbarnagar Bazar'. Residents of Mirarchar village objected, claiming the market was built jointly by both villages in 1991.

// The conflict escalated on Monday after a minor rickshaw accident triggered fresh tensions, leading to arson, vandalism, and the temporary suspension of train services on the Bhairab-Mymensingh route.

// For over three decades, the market had been managed through an unwritten agreement where leadership roles were shared between the two villages. This harmony was shattered by the sign, creating deep social and economic divisions.
// Akbarnagar residents argue the market is located within their village boundaries and officially known as Akbarnagar Bus Stand. They insist the sign should not be changed.
// Mirarchar residents maintain that the joint effort in establishing the market makes the exclusion of their name from the official signboard an insult to their history.
// Local businesses have suffered as customers now choose shops based on the village identity of the owner, and many traders from both villages have left the market.
